1.q: בִּ⁠שְׁנַת־שֶׁ֤בַע לְ⁠יֵהוּא֙ מָלַ֣ךְ יְהוֹאָ֔שׁ וְ⁠אַרְבָּעִ֣ים שָׁנָ֔ה מָלַ֖ךְ בִּ⁠ירֽוּשָׁלִָ֑ם וְ⁠שֵׁ֣ם אִמּ֔⁠וֹ צִבְיָ֖ה מִ⁠בְּאֵ֥ר שָֽׁבַע
1.note: In this verse and the next two verses, the author is introducing **Joash** as a participant in the story as the new king of Judah. To translate this verse, see how you translated the similar expressions in 8:16.

If your language would not represent a number in a form such as **seven**, you could represent this number in a form that your language would use. Alternate translation: [In the seventh year of Jehu’s reign]

The author is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [was Zibiah, and she was from Beersheba]

2.q: וַ⁠יַּ֨עַשׂ יְהוֹאָ֧שׁ הַ⁠יָּשָׁ֛ר בְּ⁠עֵינֵ֥י יְהוָ֖ה כָּל־יָמָ֑י⁠ו אֲשֶׁ֣ר הוֹרָ֔⁠הוּ יְהוֹיָדָ֖ע הַ⁠כֹּהֵֽן
2.note: If it would be more natural in your language, you could reverse the order of these phrases, since the second phrase gives the reason for the result that the first phrase describes. Alternate translation: [And because Jehoiada the priest instructed him, Joash did right in the eyes of Yahweh all of his days]
See how you translated the similar expression in 1:13. Alternate translation: [what Yahweh considered to be right]

3.note: The author is using the pronoun **they** in a general sense, not to refer to specific people. Use an expression for this that would be natural in your language. Alternate translation: [the high places were not removed]

4.note: The expression **is brought** is a passive verbal form. If your language would not use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that would be natural in your language. Alternate translation: [that people bring]
See how you translated the similar expression in 5:18. Alternate translation: [into the temple of Yahweh]

Joash is using **the silver passing over a man** as a common expression of his culture to mean the money that each Israelite male would pay during a census for the maintenance of the temple. (This was commanded in the law of Moses in Exodus 30:11–16 and originally supported the worship in the tabernacle.) If this phrase does not have that meaning in your language, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [the silver collected during a census] or [census money]

Joash is referring to **silver** that someone would pay to redeem a person or animal that he had dedicated to Yahweh, as described in Leviticus 27:1–13. You could indicate this explicitly in your translation if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [silver paid to redeem people or animals dedicated to Yahweh]

4.q: כָּל־כֶּ֗סֶף אֲשֶׁ֤ר יַֽעֲלֶה֙ עַ֣ל לֶב־אִ֔ישׁ לְ⁠הָבִ֖יא בֵּ֥ית יְהוָֽה
4.note: Joash is speaking as if **silver** could actually go **up onto the heart of a man**. He is using the heart to represent a person’s desires. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [all of the silver that a person desired to bring into the temple of Yahweh]

5.note: See how you translated the similar expression in 3:23. Alternate translation: [each of you from his acquaintances]
It might seem that this expression contains extra information that would not be natural to express in your language. If so, you can shorten it. Alternate translation: [where damage is found]

The expression **is found** is a passive verbal form. If your language would not use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that would be natural in your language. Alternate translation: [where they find damage]

6.note: The author is using this phrase to introduce a new development within this event. See how you translated the same phrase in 2:9.

6.q: בִּ⁠שְׁנַ֨ת עֶשְׂרִ֧ים וְ⁠שָׁלֹ֛שׁ שָׁנָ֖ה לַ⁠מֶּ֣לֶךְ יְהוֹאָ֑שׁ
6.note: See how you translated the similar expression in 8:25. Alternate translation: [And in the twenty-third year of King Joash]

7.note: King Joash is using the question form to express frustration and to rebuke the priests for their failure to repair the temple. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for that purpose, you could translate this as a statement or as an exclamation. Alternate translation: [You have not been successful in strengthening the damage of the house.]

**And now** was an expression that speakers in this culture commonly used to introduce an important point such as the implications of what they were just saying. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation. See how you translated this expression in 3:23.

9.note: Here the masculine term **man** has a generic sense that includes both men and women. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could use language in your translation that is clearly inclusive of both men and women. Alternate translation: [a person]

The expression **brought** is a passive verbal form. If your language would not use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that would be natural in your language. Alternate translation: [that he brought]

10.note: See how you translated the similar expression in 12:5. Alternate translation: [that they found]

11.note: The expression **was weighed** is a passive verbal form. If your language would not use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that would be natural in your language. Alternate translation: [that they had weighed]
See how you translated the similar expression in 5:5. Alternate translation: [into the custody of]

The expression **appointed** is a passive verbal form. If your language would not use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that would be natural in your language. Alternate translation: [the ones whom the king and high priest had appointed]

12.note: The author is using **everything that came out** as a common expression of his culture to describe further needs that were discovered in the process of making repairs to the temple. If this phrase does not have that meaning in your language, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and for anything else that came up as they were repairing the temple] or [and for further needs that were discovered in the process of making repairs to the temple]

The author is using the possessive form to describe **stones** that were characterized by **hewing**. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. If you have already translated the book of 1 Kings, see how you translated the similar expression in 1 Kings 5:17. Alternate translation: [and stones that workers had cut into shape]

13.q: אַךְ֩ לֹ֨א יֵעָשֶׂ֜ה בֵּ֣ית יְהוָ֗ה סִפּ֥וֹת כֶּ֨סֶף֙ מְזַמְּר֤וֹת מִזְרָקוֹת֙ חֲצֹ֣צְר֔וֹת כָּל־כְּלִ֥י זָהָ֖ב וּ⁠כְלִי־כָ֑סֶף מִן־הַ⁠כֶּ֖סֶף הַ⁠מּוּבָ֥א בֵית־יְהוָֽה
13.note: If it would be more natural in your language, you could you could combine this verse and the first sentence of the next verse into a verse bridge in which that sentence comes first, since that sentence gives the reason for the result that this verse describes. Alternate translation: [However, since they gave the silver brought to the house of Yahweh to the people doing the work, that silver was not used to make bowls of silver, snuffers, basins, trumpets, or any or articles of gold or articles of silver for the house of Yahweh]

13.q: לֹ֨א יֵעָשֶׂ֜ה & סִפּ֥וֹת כֶּ֨סֶף֙ מְזַמְּר֤וֹת מִזְרָקוֹת֙ חֲצֹ֣צְר֔וֹת כָּל־כְּלִ֥י זָהָ֖ב וּ⁠כְלִי־כָ֑סֶף
13.note: The expression **were not made** contains a passive verbal form. If your language would not use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that would be natural in your language. Alternate translation: [the workers did not make bowls of silver, snuffers, basins, trumpets, or any other articles of gold or articles of silver]
See how you translated the similar expression in 12:9. Alternate translation: [that people brought]

15.q: וְ⁠לֹ֧א יְחַשְּׁב֣וּ אֶת־הָ⁠אֲנָשִׁ֗ים אֲשֶׁ֨ר יִתְּנ֤וּ אֶת־הַ⁠כֶּ֨סֶף֙ עַל־יָדָ֔⁠ם לָ⁠תֵ֖ת לְ⁠עֹשֵׂ֣י הַ⁠מְּלָאכָ֑ה כִּ֥י בֶ⁠אֱמֻנָ֖ה הֵ֥ם עֹשִֽׂים
15.note: If it would be more natural in your language, you could reverse the order of these phrases, since the second phrase gives the reason for the result that the first phrase describes. Alternate translation: [And because the men into whose hand they gave the silver to give to the doers of the work were acting in faithfulness, they did not reckon with them]
See how you translated the similar expression in 12:11. Alternate translation: [into whose custody]

In this verse, the word **hand** is singular in form, but it refers to the hands of all of the men who had been appointed to supervise the work. If you decide to keep the image of a **hand** that represents custody, if it would be helpful in your language, you could use the plural form of the word. Alternate translation: [into whose hands]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **faithfulness**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [faithfully]

16.q: כֶּ֤סֶף אָשָׁם֙ וְ⁠כֶ֣סֶף חַטָּא֔וֹת לֹ֥א יוּבָ֖א בֵּ֣ית יְהוָ֑ה
16.note: The expression **was not brought** contains a passive verbal form. If your language would not use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that would be natural in your language. Alternate translation: [The priests did not bring the silver of the guilt offering and the silver of the sin offerings into the house of Yahweh]

If it would be more natural in your language, you could use a singular form for this expression, since it refers to the **silver** described in the previous sentence. Alternate translation: [It was to the priests] or [It belonged to the priests]

17.note: The author is using the term **Then** to introduce a new event in the story. Use a word, phrase, or other method in your language that is natural for introducing a new event.
See how you translated the similar expression in 1:3. Alternate translation: [went … to go]

The author is using **set his face** as a common expression of his culture to mean “determined.” If this phrase does not have that meaning in your language, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [And Hazael determined] or [And Hazael resolved]

18.note: See how you translated the similar expression in 8:24. Alternate translation: [his ancestors]

The author is using the term **found** in a way characteristic of his language and culture to mean that this **gold** could be found, that is, that it was present in the **treasuries** of the temple and palace. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and all of the gold that was]

19.q: וְ⁠יֶ֛תֶר דִּבְרֵ֥י יוֹאָ֖שׁ וְ⁠כָל־אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשָׂ֑ה הֲ⁠לוֹא־הֵ֣ם כְּתוּבִ֗ים עַל־סֵ֛פֶר דִּבְרֵ֥י הַ⁠יָּמִ֖ים לְ⁠מַלְכֵ֥י יְהוּדָֽה
19.note: In this verse and the next two verses, the author is concluding the story of Joash. To translate this verse, see how you translated the similar phrases in 1:18.

20.note: See how you translated the similar expression in 3:24. Alternate translation: [And his servants took action]

The author is using a construction in which a verb and its object come from the same root. You may be able to use the same construction in your language to express the meaning here. Alternatively, your language may have another way of saying this. Alternate translation: [and they formed a conspiracy]
See how you translated the similar expression in 3:24. Alternate translation: [and they attacked]

21.note: Here the author is using the pronoun **they** in a general sense, not to refer to specific people. Use an expression for this that would be natural in your language. Alternate translation: [and people buried him] or [and he was buried]
See how you translated the similar expression in 8:24. Alternate translation: [with his ancestors] or [in the same place where people had buried his ancestors]
